title: Choose your strategic bets and what you won't do
summary: Strategy is choosing where to play and how to win, and saying no to the rest. Pick a few bets that tackle the core challenge, and write down what you are stopping.

beginner: List the options that could tackle the core challenge.
For each, write where you would play and how you would win.
Pick no more than three bets.
Write down what you will not do, and why.
Note what must be true for each bet to work.
intermediate: Compare options against the diagnosis and your capabilities.
Test the riskiest assumption behind each bet quickly.
Agree the guiding approach that links the bets together.
experienced: Make choices that cut across teams and budgets.
Stop or shrink work that doesn't fit, and say so openly.
Balance bold bets with protecting the core business.

toolExamples.miro: Compare options side by side against the diagnosis.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish the chosen bets and the stop list together.

definitionOfDone: No more than three bets chosen
Key assumptions noted for each bet
pitfalls: Bets that don't address the diagnosis

sources.title: The big lie of strategic planning (Roger Martin, Harvard Business Review)
